data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Secure enclaves provide additional isolation guarantees not present in pure cryptographic commitments.","Secure enclaves may introduce performance overheads not present in software-only solutions."],"overturn_conditions":["A vulnerability in the secure enclave is discovered.","The enclave's hardware is deprecated or replaced."],"shared_structure":["Both secure enclaves and cryptographic commitments rely on computational hardness to enforce immutability.","Both provide tamper-evident guarantees."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_005"],"transfer_claims":["If a secure enclave can prevent tampering with a log, it can also turn divergence into a contradiction."]},"claim":"A hardware-enforced secure enclave (e.g., Intel SGX) is the sole durable binding that turns silent divergence into a contradiction.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The secure enclave is compromised (e.g., side-channel attacks).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log's state is not fully captured within the enclave.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The replay environment does not verify the enclave's signature.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The enclave's security guarantees are later invalidated.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The secure enclave cryptographically signs the log's state at publication, ensuring that any divergence during replay would require breaking the enclave's security guarantees, thus creating a contradiction.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
